_doc: Hand-kept input of tools/seaslug_lookalikes.py (its doc says how each field is used): the subject's root groups and area (as tools/seaslug_source.json), the floors that list a pair and that join species into an iNaturalist group, and the literature sets, each with its source, a quote and what was read (rule C2). Survey: docs/reviews/2026-11-17-seaslug-lookalikes-survey.md. Candidates only: not read by the game.

sets.source: Tibiriçá et al. 2023, as WoRMS cites it; decided by Pierre, 2026-11-15, Q377 (tools/seaslugs.json lookalikes)
sets.quote: The two Spanish dancers: pages and Wikipedia say 'Spanish dancer' for either; WoRMS accepts both
sets.note: already in play: the one decided pair

sets.source: Rudman W.B. 1999 (July 6), Sea Slug Forum message 'Juvenile Hexabranchus from Philippines', http://www.seaslugforum.net/find/1013 (a juvenile from Dauin, then named H. sanguineus; the juveniles of iNaturalist are H. lacer: docs/reviews/2026-11-15-seaslug-sources.md 1.5)
sets.quote: It has a remarkable resemblance to some purple spotted chromodorids such as Hypselodoris maculosa, Thorunna australis and Chromodoris decora.
sets.note: the juvenile only: a photo-level pair (its juvenile photos), not the adult

sets.source: Rudman W.B. 1998 (November 29), Sea Slug Forum fact sheet Chromodoris willani, https://www.seaslugforum.net/find/chrowill
sets.quote: similarly coloured species with a bluish white or translucent white background colour ... Other species include Chromodoris lochi, Chromodoris boucheti and Chromodoris dianae.
sets.note: C. boucheti is a synonym of C. lochi in the list (tools/seaslugs.json syn)

sets.source: Rudman W.B. 1998 (November 19), Sea Slug Forum fact sheet Chromodoris annae, https://www.seaslugforum.net/find/chroanna
sets.quote: This species has similarities to Chromodoris elisabethina but C. annae is characterised by the dark specks in the blue areas ... The only other chromodorid with similar pitted blue regions is Chromodoris westraliensis.

sets.source: Layton K.K.S., Carvajal J.I. & Wilson N.G. 2020. Mimicry and mitonuclear discordance in nudibranchs: new insights from exon capture phylogenomics. Ecology and Evolution 10: 11966-11982, https://doi.org/10.1002/ece3.6727 (PMC7664011)
sets.quote: the “magnifica” morph of C. joshi (C. joshi × magnifica)
sets.note: C. joshi can wear C. magnifica's pattern; the paper reads it as mitonuclear discordance, not mimicry

sets.quote: had the mitogenome of C. elisabethina but with the nuclear signal and color pattern of C. annae

sets.source: Rudman W.B. 1999 (January 12), Sea Slug Forum fact sheet Phyllidia varicosa, after Brunckhorst 1993, https://www.seaslugforum.net/find/phylvari
sets.quote: Phyllidia tula has a longitudinal black stripe on its foot, but the foot is very dark grey ... Phyllidia coelestis is a smaller species which has neither a foot stripe nor a median ridge.

sets.source: Rudman W.B. 1999, Sea Slug Forum fact sheet Phyllidia elegans, after Brunckhorst 1993, https://www.seaslugforum.net/find/phyleleg
sets.quote: [P. varicosa and P. tula] both have a black line on the foot sole, but neither has pink coloration nor black lines on the sides of the foot.

sets.source: Stoffels B.E.M.W. et al. 2016. Phylogenetic relationships within the Phyllidiidae. ZooKeys 605: 1-35, https://doi.org/10.3897/zookeys.605.7136 (PMC4978068)
sets.quote: [Brunckhorst (1993)] already noticed the close similarity between the two species but still confused them
Phyllidiella rudmani and P. lizae resemble each other

sets.source: Rudman W.B. 1999 (September 12), Sea Slug Forum fact sheet Phyllidiella pustulosa, after Brunckhorst 1993, https://www.seaslugforum.net/find/phylpust
sets.quote: Phyllidiella pustulosa is closest in appearance to Phyllidiella annulata, Phyllidiella zeylanica and Phyllidiella granulata.

sets.source: Rudman W.B. 2004 (July 23), Sea Slug Forum 'Mimicry', https://www.seaslugforum.net/mimicry.htm
sets.quote: Discodoris? liturata ... an almost perfect mimic of Phyllidiella pustulosa
sets.note: across families (Phyllidiidae, Discodorididae); the same page names a flatworm, Pseudoceros imitatus, not a sea slug

sets.source: Rudman W.B. 1999 (January 22), Sea Slug Forum fact sheet Chromodoris kuniei, https://www.seaslugforum.net/find/chrokuni
sets.quote: Other species include Risbecia tryoni, Chromodoris geminus and Chromodoris leopardus. ... C. leopardus and C. kuniei can be distinguished from R. tryoni by the broad purple border ... and by the leopard-like multiple spots
sets.note: Risbecia tryoni is Hypselodoris tryoni, Chromodoris leopardus Goniobranchus leopardus (WoRMS)

sets.source: Rudman W.B. 1999 (May 6), Sea Slug Forum fact sheet Hypselodoris bullocki, https://www.seaslugforum.net/find/hypsbull; English Wikipedia, Hypselodoris bullockii
sets.quote: See Hypselodoris apolegma, which may be a colour form.

sets.source: Epstein H.C. et al. 2019. Reading between the lines: revealing cryptic species diversity and colour patterns in Hypselodoris nudibranchs. Zool. J. Linn. Soc. 186: 116-189, https://doi.org/10.1093/zoolinnean/zly048; California Academy of Sciences news release, 2018-10-29, https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/818323
sets.quote: [the lavender form of H. iba] looked strikingly similar to another purple species common to the region
sets.read: the news release; the paper's abstract through a search result
sets.note: Mullerian mimicry (the abstract, as the search result gives it)

sets.source: Rudman W.B. 2008 (March 2), Sea Slug Forum fact sheet Nembrotha kubaryana, https://www.seaslugforum.net/find/nembkuba
sets.quote: A similarly coloured species, Nembrotha cristata lacks the orange border to the foot.

sets.source: Rudman W.B. 2007 (July 27), Sea Slug Forum message 'Chromodoris dianae vs. C. lochi', https://www.seaslugforum.net/find/20016
sets.quote: The key difference between C. dianae and C. lochi is not the rhinophore colour ... the small white specks all over the mantle in C. dianae

sets.source: Rudman W.B. 2000 (February 10), Sea Slug Forum 'Chromodoris decora Colour Group: How to differentiate the species', https://seaslugforum.net/find/chrodeco1
sets.quote: translucent or very pale colours with thin white longitudinal lines on the mantle ... There is no suggestion that species of a colour group are necessarily closely related
sets.read: the page (its photo legend; the cf. forms left out)

sets.source: Nudi Pixel, 'Nudibranch Look-Alikes', https://nudipixel.net/similarities (read 2026-11-17; cite only)

sets.note: a mimicry set across three families
Pearsonothuria graeffei is a sea cucumber (its juvenile), not a sea slug
